elements_not_encoded.text: If abdominal aortic aneurysm likely: avoid giving IV fluids even if BP < 90/60 (raising blood pressure may worsen rupture).
If BP < 90/60 or pancreatitis likely, give sodium chloride 0.9% 500mL IV over 30 minutes, repeat until systolic BP > 90. Continue 1L 6 hourly. Stop if breathing
If complicated pyelonephritis likely: first collect urine for MCS and then give ceftriaxone 1g IV2/IM.
If kidney stone likely: give sodium chloride 0.9% 1L IV 6 hourly. If pain severe, give morphine 5-10mg IM or diluted morphine 3-5mg IV. If giving IV, dilute 10m
If patient known to have cancer, refer same day.

judgment_calls.decision: One probable Acute pyelonephritis rule (flank pain + leucocytes/nitrites); the complicating factors are written directly into the Urgent priority rule.
judgment_calls.alternatives: Two diagnosis rules with the same concept; a priority on active_condition pyelonephritis (would make uncomplicated cases urgent).

judgment_calls.topic: Recent injury and x-ray unavailable or abnormal
judgment_calls.decision: Encoded as Traumatic injury only; recency and the x-ray condition are not expressible.
judgment_calls.alternatives: Drop the item (would miss urgent injuries).

judgment_calls.decision: Not encoded: no inflammatory back pain concept, none of the Q3 criteria is expressible, and age > 50 / < 40 has no form.
judgment_calls.alternatives: Probable Mechanical low back pain on (no) of the Q1/Q2 items, which would also fire for inflammatory back pain.

judgment_calls.decision: Possible Tuberculosis when back pain with cough, weight loss, night sweats or fever.
Inguinal pain stands in for "radiating to groin"; one-sided as Unilateral qualifier on flank pain.
Footnote 1 written inline on this page as an or of SBP < 80, pulse >= 100, RR > 30, Acute confusion.
judgment_calls.alternatives: A shared sepsis definition (excluded by the brief).
